title: Bleibst du?
desc: Asked over potatoes, which is how the big ones arrive
setting: A kitchen on a Sunday, two knives, and a question that has been waiting since November.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Und bist du im Juli überhaupt noch da?
steps.en: And will you even still be here in July?

options.feedback: She has asked since November and you have not answered since November. A question back is the fourth dodge.

options.es: Mein Vertrag läuft im September aus.
options.en: My contract runs out in September.
options.feedback: The real fact, said out loud for the first time. She already knew the date. You had never spoken it.

options.en: Of course I am still here.
options.feedback: Warm and it skips the paperwork. Staying here is a contract and a permit, not a feeling.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Ich frage seit November. Du antwortest nicht.
steps.en: I have been asking since November. You do not answer.

options.feedback: She is. Three times she asked and three times you heard a different question.
True, and it is not much of a defence. She noticed all three times.

options.en: I did not have an answer.
options.feedback: Also true, and it is the honest version of the same thing. She will take it.
One word, said before you have thought about it, and still true two minutes later. That is the answer.
She will say that is not the question. Between wanting and doing there is a great deal of paper.
The honest answer for a year. She is asking whether it is still the honest answer today.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.en: Then we have to do something.

options.feedback: She is already getting a sheet of paper. A list here is a declaration; joining in on it is the answer.
Twenty minutes after the biggest question of your life, yes. That is not coldness, it is how it is meant.
Said as a joke and it is also true. Somebody who makes a list has already decided.
